bead.title: Implement typed range scans and stable cursor pagination
bead.description:
PROBLEM
Detail pages and due-work queries need typed range scans and stable cursor pagination over compound indexes. Current typed index lookup is exact-key oriented and does not provide ordered range pages.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement memory and sqlite support for bounded typed range scans over declared compound indexes, including stable ordering by `(scheduled_at ASC, action_id ASC)` and cursor page tokens or an explicit retryable cursor-invalidated error. Expose through the public facade query API added earlier.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- crates/pqueue-projection/src/lib.rs for in-memory projection range scan support.
- crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs for sqlite range scan support.
- crates/pqueue/src/lib.rs and crates/pqueue/tests/hot_projection_queries.rs.

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Grouped aggregates.
- Bounded mutation.
- Claim-by-query.

ORDERING/TIE-BREAK
Stable ordering and the cursor tie-break must follow the contract decision in pqueue-b1feb686: `action_id` is not a field of the canonical range index, so either the implementation tie-breaks on the internal item id or the test's declared index is extended — implement whichever the contract specifies, and make the test assert that behavior explicitly. In the canonical fixture, ordering by (scheduled_at ASC, internal id ASC) and (scheduled_at ASC, action_id ASC) yield the same page sequence.
bead.acceptance:
1. `cargo test -p pqueue --test hot_projection_queries ordered_cursor_pagination_is_stable -- --nocapture` passes and returns pages `[act_001, act_002]`, `[act_003, act_004]`, `[act_005]` for `message.send`.
2. The same test inserts an unrelated later row between page fetches and proves no duplicate/skip of already-visible rows, or gets the documented retryable cursor-invalidated error.
3. `cargo test -p pqueue --test hot_projection_queries detail_range_filter_by_run_status_and_schedule -- --nocapture` passes.
4. `cargo fmt --check` passes.
